airvault-guideTitle: How to verify your dice-generated BIP39 words manually
airvault-diceBasic: Roll a physical six-sided die. Enter the number you rolled below. Rolls 1, 2, or 3 become 0; rolls 4, 5, or 6 become 1. After 11 rolls, check the result and add the word to your prefix.
airvault-fairDice: Use a fair physical die and independent rolls. Do not invent a pattern or repeatedly click a number. This mapping is unbiased only when the two groups are equally likely.
airvault-generatorBasic: Name your wallet, choose a phrase length and entropy method, and record your prefix words. The default is 11 dice-generated words plus operating-system randomness for a 24-word phrase. Review each word, generate the full phrase, write it down privately, then hide and re-enter it to finish.
airvault-fullDiceHelp: Each die roll supplies one entropy bit. Enter 256 rolls for a 24-word phrase, or 128 for a 12-word phrase. AirVault then computes the checksum. Do not roll an independent final word.
airvault-invalidRoll: Enter a whole die value from 1 to 6.
airvault-tooManyRolls: This group is complete. Undo or reset before entering another roll.
airvault-elevenRolls: Exactly 11 rolls are required for one word.
airvault-invalidWord: Enter one word from the BIP39 English list.
airvault-checkboxHelp: This checkbox records your own check. It is not cryptographic proof of independent verification.
airvault-independentList: Check against an independently obtained copy of the official wordlist when possible. A list bundled in the same app cannot independently establish that the app itself is trustworthy.
airvault-findWord: Find a word or printed position
airvault-publicExample: Public example — never use this as wallet entropy
airvault-manualSteps:
1. Roll an ordinary six-sided die 11 times.
2. Write down each result in the order rolled.
3. Convert each roll: 1, 2, 3 become 0; 4, 5, 6 become 1.
4. Write the 11 binary digits in the same order.
5. Assign these weights, from left to right:
   1024 512 256 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1
6. Add the weights whose bit is 1. Ignore weights whose bit is 0.
7. The total is the word's zero-based index (0–2047).
8. Add 1 for a printed list numbered 1–2048.
9. Find that position in the official BIP39 English wordlist.
10. Compare its word with AirVault's result.

If they match, you have independently checked the dice-to-word mapping.
airvault-advancedEntropy: BIP39 encodes ENT + ENT/32 bits in 11-bit word indices. A 24-word phrase has 256 entropy bits and 8 checksum bits; a 12-word phrase has 128 entropy bits and 4 checksum bits. SHA-256 of the entropy supplies the leading checksum bits. The final word contains entropy and checksum bits, so it cannot be chosen as an independent word.
airvault-advancedPrefix: Prefix words preserve their full 11-bit indices, including leading zeroes. The default 11-word prefix uses 121 of 256 bits; the OS CSPRNG fills the remaining 135 bits before the checksum is appended. Up to 23 prefix words are allowed for 24 words, or 11 for 12 words. Human-chosen words may have much less entropy than random dice rolls.
airvault-secretWorksheet: Your actual rolls and word calculations remain available only during this creation ceremony. They are cleared when you finish, cancel, leave the page, or lock. They are never logged, persisted, exported, or exposed through MCP. JavaScript and operating-system memory cannot be guaranteed to erase every historical copy.
airvault-basicVault:
1. Create a vault with a unique password of at least six characters. AirVault starts offline.
2. Open Wallets to generate or import a recovery phrase. Record a generated phrase and complete its verification.
3. Open Accounts and choose a blockchain. You can include a token on supported token networks.
4. For one computer, choose Online in Settings. For separate computers, use Offline on the signer and Proxy on the connected computer.
5. Export public accounts (.avpub) to the proxy, then prepare and export a transfer request (.avreq).
6. Import the request on the signer, review the transaction, approve signing, and export .avsig.
7. Import .avsig on the connected computer, review it, and approve broadcast.
airvault-advancedVault: Each signing request binds the blockchain, sender, native operation and transaction parameters. AirVault reconstructs the native transaction, requires local approval, signs it, and verifies its signatures and exact contents before export. Bitcoin-family inputs include complete previous transactions. Polkadot transfers bind runtime metadata into their signatures.
airvault-advancedProvider: Choose Online or Proxy in Settings and set a provider for each network you use. Provider requests occur only after an explicit action. Use separate profiles for an offline signer and a watch-only proxy.
airvault-basicBackup: Create an encrypted backup in Settings and test restoring it into a new profile. Keep the vault password, optional custom root passwords and BIP39 passphrases available separately. A forgotten BIP39 passphrase cannot be recovered from the mnemonic; each passphrase derives a different wallet.
airvault-helpOffline: All instructions, the public example and the wordlist below work offline. Open the official link in a separate online browser. Never paste actual recovery words into a website.

airvault-previewScope: AirVault stores and signs keys locally. Keep an encrypted backup and verify your recovery phrases before relying on them.
airvault-secureVaultHelp: Use a long, unique password or a few randomly chosen words. Keep it somewhere safe: it cannot be recovered for you. AirVault starts offline; you can choose Online or Proxy in Settings.
airvault-strengthHelp: This local estimate considers common passwords, words, repeats, sequences, keyboard patterns and length. Character variety helps, but predictable substitutions do not make a password random. The grade is advisory; any password of at least six characters is accepted.
airvault-externalHelp: Balances, unspent status, recent block references and network fee estimates come from the provider. Verify them on the connected wallet before broadcasting.
airvault-invalidAmount: Enter a positive amount within the asset’s decimal precision.
airvault-transferHelp: Enter the recipient and amount. Load network data to fill account counters, block references and inputs, then review the resulting transaction before signing. You can also enter these fields manually from your connected wallet.
airvault-copySeedWarning: Other apps and clipboard history may be able to read it. Copy only on a trusted device, then clear the clipboard and its history when finished.
airvault-phraseFormat: Use full words or their first four letters, separated by spaces or lines. Numbered words must be one per line: 1. word.
airvault-deleteAccountHelp: This removes the saved account and its token list from this vault. Your wallet, signing identities, transaction history and funds stay intact. To add it again, use the same wallet, identity, network and derivation path, or reimport its public account file. For multisig, save the complete configuration and address index first; the recovery phrase alone is not enough to recreate the shared address.

airvault-page_accounts: A wallet holds the recovery secret. An account is a blockchain address derived from that wallet and a signing identity. One wallet can have many accounts, including accounts on different networks. Use this page to derive addresses, manage tokens, export public accounts or delete saved account entries.
airvault-page_transfer: Prepare a transfer from an account. Review the recipient, asset, amount and fee before creating a signing request.
airvault-page_requests: Import and review transactions to sign, or inspect signed responses. An offline signer returns a signed file to the connected computer for broadcasting.
airvault-page_history: Review the record of signing and broadcasting performed by this vault. This is local activity, not a full blockchain transaction history.
airvault-page_networks: A reference list of the blockchains and token standards available in AirVault. Create and manage your addresses under Accounts.
airvault-page_settings: Choose Offline, Online or Proxy mode; configure locking and providers; manage encrypted backups and your vault password.
airvault-page_help: Choose a topic and switch between basic steps and advanced details. These instructions are available offline.
airvault-guide_start_basic:
Create a vault with a unique password. AirVault starts in Offline mode.

Open Create or import to make a new wallet or restore a recovery phrase. Record a new phrase, hide it, then type it back to verify your backup. Find saved wallets under Wallets & recovery.

Open Accounts, select a signing identity and network, give the account a label, and choose Derive account. Use its address to receive funds on that same network.

For a single connected computer, choose Online in Settings. For two computers, keep Offline on the signer and choose Proxy on the connected computer. See Transfers & signing for the file exchange.
airvault-guide_start_advanced:
The vault encrypts root secrets and BIP39 passphrases at rest. Root wallets feed signing identities, and identities derive network accounts at explicit derivation paths.

Offline mode disables provider calls. Proxy mode stores public accounts and prepares or broadcasts transactions without holding roots. Online mode combines local signing and provider access.

Use disposable accounts and test networks to check your backup and signing workflow before receiving funds. Public account exports are watch-only but still reveal addresses and account relationships.
airvault-guide_recovery_basic:
Create or import offers a new recovery phrase, recovery phrase import, or Bitcoin WIF import. A WIF is a single private key, not a recovery phrase.

Write a generated phrase in order. Copy seed phrase asks before placing a numbered list on the clipboard; clipboard history and other apps may retain it. After hiding the phrase, enter it to verify. You can correct errors and retry until the five-minute ceremony expires. Cancel or leaving the page discards an unfinished ceremony.

Type full English words or their first four letters. Separate plain words with spaces or new lines. Numbered entries must be one per line, in sequence, such as 1. abandon then 2. ability on the next line. Do not place numbered entries together on one line. Three-letter words such as zoo must be written in full.

Wallets & recovery checks a saved phrase against its wallet without showing the stored phrase. A failed check keeps your text so you can fix typos.
airvault-guide_recovery_advanced:
AirVault accepts 12- and 24-word English BIP39 phrases and validates their checksum after expanding unique four-letter prefixes. Numbered input is interpreted only as sequential, one-word-per-line entries. Invalid spellings are rejected, not autocorrected.

OS randomness generates the entropy locally. Manual-prefix mode preserves the selected leading word bits and fills the remaining entropy with OS randomness. Full entropy uses exactly 128 or 256 physical dice bits; the BIP39 checksum is computed afterward.

A generated phrase is held in memory for up to five minutes. Incorrect confirmation does not consume it; successful persistence, cancellation, lock or expiry ends the ceremony. Recovery verification compares canonical words against the encrypted root.
airvault-guide_accounts_basic:
Your wallet is the recovery secret. A signing identity uses that wallet either on its own or with a BIP39 passphrase. An account is an address on a specific blockchain, derived from an identity.

In Accounts, select the identity, enter a label and choose a network. Leave the derivation path at its suggested value unless you are restoring an address with a known different path. Derive account creates the address locally.

Copy shares the address for receiving funds. Export public accounts shares addresses for use in a Proxy vault, without private keys. Treat the export as private information because it links your addresses.

Delete account asks for confirmation and removes the saved address and token list. It does not move funds or remove the wallet. Record the identity, network and path first so you can derive it again. A watch-only account can be reimported.
airvault-guide_accounts_advanced:
The derivation path selects a branch and index under a signing identity. Different paths can produce different addresses from the same root. Use the exact network, identity and path when recovering an account; changing a label has no cryptographic effect.

Public-account bundles contain addresses, public keys, paths and token metadata. They confer no signing power but can expose financial relationships. Verify exported addresses against your signer before receiving funds.

Deleting an account preserves roots, identities, pending requests and activity. Any outstanding signing approval is invalidated; requests need a fresh review. Recreate the account before signing a pending request that depends on it, and re-add any token metadata.
airvault-guide_passphrases_basic:
A BIP39 passphrase creates a different identity from the same recovery phrase. Open Passphrases, select a wallet, name the identity and enter its passphrase. You can then select that identity in Accounts.

Every character matters, including spaces and capitalization. A typo creates a different identity, so record and check the passphrase carefully. The recovery phrase alone cannot recover accounts created with a passphrase.

Keep the passphrase backup separate from the recovery phrase. A custom root password, if used, unlocks the stored root; it is a different password with a different purpose.
airvault-guide_passphrases_advanced:
BIP39 derives a seed from the mnemonic and normalized passphrase. Different passphrases create different seeds; there is no checksum that identifies a correct passphrase. AirVault encrypts the stored passphrase as part of the identity.

The vault password protects the vault file. An optional custom root password wraps an individual root secret. A BIP39 passphrase changes derivation. These three credentials are not interchangeable; keep a tested recovery plan for each.

Restore the same mnemonic, exact BIP39 passphrase, network and derivation path to reproduce an address. Verify a known address after restoring, before using it.
airvault-guide_signing_basic:
Online mode prepares and signs on one computer. Offline plus Proxy separates those steps across two computers.

Export public accounts from the signer, then import the .avpub file on the Proxy. Prepare a transfer there and export the .avreq signing request. Use Import on the signer, then open Signing requests.

Review the network, every recipient, amount, asset and fee. Approve with your vault password and any custom root passwords. Export the .avsig response, import it on the connected computer, review it and broadcast.

Activity records local signing and broadcast events. Check confirmation status with your network provider; signing alone does not send funds.
airvault-guide_signing_advanced:
Treat request files and provider data as untrusted. Transaction review is derived from the transaction bytes; a friendly description is context only. Check token contract or mint addresses as well as symbols.

Approval is bound to a reviewed request and expires after two minutes. Failed or completed signing consumes that approval; open a fresh review to retry. Recovery-phrase confirmation has a separate five-minute retry window.

Network state such as nonce, blockhash, UTXOs, fees and runtime metadata can become stale during offline transport. Rebuild and review a fresh request when the network rejects expired state. Retain request and response files until you have verified the broadcast result.
airvault-guide_security_basic:
Use a unique vault password of at least six characters. The strength meter is guidance; it does not block weak passwords that meet the minimum. A longer unpredictable password or passphrase is safer.

An optional custom root password adds protection to a single wallet inside the vault. It does not replace the recovery phrase or change the wallet's addresses. Back it up if you use it.

Create an encrypted backup in Settings. Test restoring it into a new profile with its vault password. A recovery phrase restores wallet secrets; an encrypted vault backup also keeps account metadata and stored identities.

Keep recovery phrases and BIP39 passphrases safely backed up. Avoid copying secrets when possible, and clear clipboard history after copying. Automatic locking limits how long secrets remain available while the app is open.
airvault-guide_security_advanced:
Vault encryption uses Argon2id to derive a key and AES-256-GCM to authenticate encrypted data. A strong unique password protects a stolen backup; interface lock settings do not compensate for a weak password.

Custom root passwords protect individual encrypted roots. BIP39 passphrases are separate derivation inputs. Losing either can prevent access through the vault, and losing a BIP39 passphrase prevents phrase-only recovery of that identity.

Restore into a fresh profile, verify known addresses and check necessary passphrase identities. The dry-run restore option checks a backup without installing it. Preserve older known-good backups when changing credentials.

Choose trusted provider endpoints in Settings. Provider access reveals queried addresses and transaction metadata. Offline mode disables those calls but does not secure an otherwise compromised computer.
airvault-guide_networks_basic:
Cryptocurrencies lists the networks you can use. Accounts is where you create an address on one of those networks.

Tokens live on a blockchain. ERC-20 tokens can be included when creating an Ethereum account, or added to an existing account. Enter the correct contract or mint address, symbol and decimals for the chosen network.

Always match the sender and recipient network. Similar-looking addresses do not mean funds can be sent across networks. Test coins are separate from main-network funds.
airvault-guide_networks_advanced:
EVM networks can share address formats while using different chain IDs and assets. Verify both the chain and token contract. A symbol is only display metadata; it does not prove token identity.

Token standards describe transaction formats: ERC-20 on EVM networks, SPL on Solana and TRC-20 on Tron. Contract or mint addresses and decimals determine how token quantities are interpreted.

Derivation defaults follow each adapter's supported wallet convention. Preserve exact paths when recovering from another wallet. Provider state and transaction formats differ by chain; inspect the resulting transaction before signing.
airvault-guide_dice_basic:
Use a fair physical six-sided die and enter each actual roll. Rolls 1, 2 or 3 give bit 0; rolls 4, 5 or 6 give bit 1. Eleven rolls select one BIP39 word.

Do not invent rolls or click a pattern. Follow the worked example below to independently check each word.
airvault-guide_dice_advanced:
The mapping is unbiased when the two groups of outcomes are equally likely and rolls are independent. Eleven bits address the 2,048-word English list, with a zero-based index from 0 to 2,047.

Manual prefix words supply fixed leading entropy bits. The app supplies the remaining entropy from the operating system. Full-entropy entry needs 128 or 256 bits; the final phrase also contains checksum bits, so independently rolled complete word sequences are not automatically valid BIP39 phrases.
airvault-ceremonyExpired: The recovery phrase expired. Generate a new phrase to continue.
airvault-page_about: Identify this build and compare the SHA-256 of the running application file with a checksum from a trusted source.
airvault-clipboardFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard. Select the hash and copy it manually.
airvault-hashInvalid: Enter a SHA-256 checksum: exactly 64 hexadecimal characters.
airvault-hashDiffers: The file does not match this checksum.
airvault-integrityHelp: The version hash identifies the source files included at build time, including local edits. The current binary hash is calculated from the running application's file each time you open this page or recalculate. Compare it with an independently trusted release checksum.
airvault-integrityLimit: A matching checksum confirms matching file bytes. It does not establish who published the file or prove that the computer is safe.
airvault-searchInstructionsHint: Try proxy, restore, fees or entropy
airvault-noArticles: No matching articles. Try a shorter word.
airvault-whitepaperTitle: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
airvault-whitepaperSaved: Bitcoin whitepaper saved. Open the PDF in your document reader.
airvault-whitepaperOffline: The original PDF is bundled with AirVault. Saving it needs no internet connection.
airvault-timeoutHint: -1 = Never. Closing AirVault still locks the vault.
airvault-timeoutHelp: Use -1 to disable locking from inactivity, or 30–3600 seconds for an idle timer. Manual locking, closing the app and sleep/resume still lock. “Lock on focus loss” is a separate setting.
airvault-modeOfflineHelp: Offline keeps private keys on this computer and blocks blockchain provider requests. Use it for the signer in a two-computer setup. Physical isolation requires disconnecting the computer.
airvault-modeOnlineHelp: Online prepares, signs and broadcasts on this computer. Private keys and network access are in the same environment.
airvault-modeProxyHelp: Proxy uses imported public accounts to prepare requests and broadcast signed responses. It cannot store root wallets or sign.
airvault-proxyDisabledRoots: Proxy is unavailable because this vault contains private keys. Use a fresh profile on the connected computer, select Proxy before adding wallets, then import the signer's .avpub file. Removing an account does not remove its private root.
airvault-proxyDisabledBuild: This build has no network capability, so Online and Proxy are unavailable.
airvault-entropyOsHelp: OS randomness: quick and automatic. All entropy comes from the operating system's secure random generator; you rely on the computer and its random source.
airvault-entropyMixedHelp: Manual prefix + OS randomness: you provide the leading words, then the OS fills the remaining entropy. You can check the manual part, but predictable words weaken that part. More manual words mean fewer OS-generated bits.
airvault-entropyRawHelp: Full entropy: you supply every entropy bit using physical dice or verified bits. This is slower and entirely depends on your source; the OS adds no randomness. AirVault adds the checksum.
airvault-entropyChangeHelp: Changing the source, phrase length or entry method clears the current entropy entry.
airvault-steps_start:
Create the vault with a password you can recover. The meter grades the password; the minimum is six characters.
Open Create or import and create a recovery phrase. For a simple first setup, choose OS randomness. Write the result down and complete verification.
Open Accounts, select the wallet identity and desired network, enter a label and derive an account.
Create and test an encrypted backup in Settings. Verify that you can reproduce a known address before relying on it.
Use Receive a payment for incoming funds. Choose Send on one computer or Offline file exchange for your sending setup.
airvault-result_start: You have an encrypted vault, a recorded recovery phrase and an account address on your chosen network.
airvault-steps_recovery:
Choose Create or import, then New recovery phrase, Import recovery phrase or Import Bitcoin WIF.
Enter a wallet label. Leave Custom root password empty unless you want a separate password for that root.
For a new phrase, select its length and entropy source, generate it, record every word in order and choose I recorded it — hide and verify.
Re-enter the words and confirm. If there is a typo, correct the existing text and retry before the five-minute ceremony expires.
For import, enter the existing phrase and Save. Open Wallets & recovery to see the saved wallet or verify its recovery phrase later.
airvault-result_recovery: A saved wallet appears with its Default identity. You can then derive accounts. A generated phrase is not shown again after confirmation.
airvault-steps_accounts:
Open Accounts and select a signing identity from a saved wallet.
Enter a label, choose Network and keep the suggested derivation path unless recovering a known different one.
For a token account, include the token's contract or mint, symbol and decimals on the matching network.
Choose Derive account. Check the saved address and open Details to record its path and identity.
Export public accounts for a Proxy, or use Copy to share the address for receiving.
airvault-result_accounts: The account is saved under its identity. Deleting the account removes this entry and token metadata, not the wallet keys or funds.
airvault-steps_passphrases:
Open Passphrases and select the root wallet.
Enter a descriptive label and the exact BIP39 passphrase. Provide the custom root password if that wallet uses one.
Choose Add passphrase identity. Back up the passphrase separately from the recovery phrase.
Open Accounts and select the new identity. Derive an address and compare it during a recovery rehearsal.
airvault-result_passphrases: The new identity appears alongside Default. Default continues to mean no additional BIP39 passphrase.
airvault-steps_signing:
Import the .avreq file, or prepare a request in Online mode, then open Signing requests.
Open Review transaction. Check network, recipients, asset identifiers, amounts, fees and change from the decoded transaction.
Enter the vault password and required custom root passwords, check the approval box and sign.
Export the signed response for the Proxy, or review and broadcast from Online mode.
Check the transaction ID on the network. Reopen review if an approval expires.
airvault-result_signing: Signing creates a response for the reviewed request. It does not broadcast until you explicitly use the broadcast action.
airvault-steps_security:
Choose a unique vault password of six or more characters. Use the strength meter to improve it without relying on character categories alone.
If you enable a custom root password, record it separately and verify that it works for the intended wallet.
Back up recovery phrases, required BIP39 passphrases and the encrypted vault. Test recovery in a fresh profile.
Set your inactivity and focus-loss policy in Settings. Use Lock vault when leaving the computer.
airvault-result_security: You know which credential protects storage and which credentials are required to reproduce each identity.
airvault-steps_networks:
Open Cryptocurrencies to see network families, then go to Accounts to create an address.
Select the network before entering token details. Obtain the token contract or mint and decimals from the asset's authoritative source.
Include the token when deriving the account or add it to the account afterward.
Check both network and asset with the sender or recipient; keep native coin available for transaction fees.
airvault-result_networks: A token is tracked under its blockchain account rather than as a separate recovery wallet.
airvault-steps_dice:
Select Manual prefix + OS randomness and Guided physical dice in Create or import.
Roll a physical die eleven times for one word. Enter each result in order; use Undo last roll for an entry mistake.
Check How was this word calculated? against your independent calculation and wordlist.
Choose Add this word, then continue with the next word. Use the separate already-generated-word section only for a word you calculated elsewhere.
Review the recorded words below the generation controls and mark the ones you independently checked.
airvault-result_dice: The app records the prefix words and their calculation details for this creation attempt. The final phrase includes any OS-filled bits and a checksum.
airvault-note_dice: Do not use the examples or repeat a pattern. Ticking a verification box records your check; it does not prove that the rolls were random.
airvault-note_accounts: An account deletion is not a blockchain operation. Funds remain controlled by the same keys, so keep the recovery information and path.
airvault-note_passphrases: There is no “wrong passphrase” checksum. A typo can produce a different valid identity with different addresses.
airvault-note_signing: Descriptions and token symbols can be misleading. Approve the decoded transaction fields and asset identifiers.
airvault-note_recovery: A numbered phrase must have one numbered word per line. “1. word 2. another” on one line is rejected. Copying a phrase may leave it in clipboard history.
airvault-guide_modes_basic:
AirVault uses the same application in all three modes. A new vault starts Offline. Choose a mode for each profile in Settings.

Offline holds your wallets and signs imported requests without contacting blockchain providers. Online combines wallet storage, preparation, signing and broadcasting on one computer. Proxy holds public accounts only; it prepares transactions and broadcasts signatures produced elsewhere.

Proxy is disabled when the vault contains private roots, including imported private keys. This prevents turning a private-key vault into a watch-only profile by changing a setting. Deleting account entries does not remove those roots.
airvault-steps_modes:
For one computer, unlock the vault and open Settings. Select Online if you want to prepare and send transfers there.
For two computers, keep the computer containing your recovery phrases Offline. Create a fresh vault on the connected computer, then select Proxy before creating or importing any private wallets.
Enter the vault password, check the settings confirmation and Save.
On the signer, export public accounts from Accounts. Import that .avpub file on the Proxy using Import file.
Check the mode badge and verify the imported address against the signer before preparing a transfer.
airvault-result_modes: Offline has no Prepare transfer page. Online can prepare and sign. Proxy can prepare transfers but hides private-wallet creation and cannot sign.
airvault-guide_modes_advanced:
Modes are enforced in the native backend, not only through navigation. Offline rejects provider calls; Proxy rejects private-root operations. Switching to Proxy is rejected while encrypted private records exist. Watch-only accounts do not provide signing keys.

Mode is persisted inside each encrypted profile. --data-dir selects a profile directory; use a different absolute directory for a new profile. For example on Windows: AirVault.exe --data-dir C:\AirVaultProfiles\Proxy. A separate directory on the same computer is useful for testing but is not an air gap.

A real offline setup needs a separate isolated signer, controlled removable media and review on the signer. The mode flag cannot prevent other software on the operating system from communicating. Builds without networking disable both connected modes.
airvault-note_modes: Do not import a recovery phrase into the Proxy. Share only public accounts. If a vault already contains roots, preserve it and create a separate profile instead.
airvault-guide_entropy_basic:
Entropy is the unpredictable starting material for a recovery phrase. Choose the source before entering dice results. AirVault offers three sources; all produce a phrase with a calculated checksum.

OS randomness is the simplest option: the operating system supplies every entropy bit. It is fast and avoids recording mistakes, but you trust the computer's secure random generator.

Manual prefix + OS randomness lets you choose how many leading words to supply from independent physical rolls. AirVault preserves those word bits and generates the remaining entropy with the OS. You can verify the manual part; it takes extra work and is weaker if your chosen words are predictable.

Full entropy uses only the bits you enter, from physical dice or an independently verified source. It avoids relying on OS randomness for the phrase but requires 128 or 256 fair, independent bits. There is no automatic random fill to compensate for a weak source.
airvault-steps_entropy:
In Create or import, choose New recovery phrase and a phrase length of 12 or 24 words.
Choose OS randomness for automatic generation, or choose a manual source if you have a way to generate and check independent random input.
For Manual prefix + OS randomness, select the number of prefix words. Use guided dice to roll each word, or enter already-generated words. The bit counter shows how much remains for the OS.
For Full entropy, enter exactly 128 bits for 12 words or 256 bits for 24 words. Guided physical dice records one bit per roll; raw input accepts a verified bit string.
Generate the phrase, record the complete result and finish the hide-and-verify step.
airvault-result_entropy: You receive one 12- or 24-word recovery phrase. Its final checksum is computed by AirVault; the checksum is not extra randomness.
airvault-guide_entropy_advanced:
Manual-prefix mode places n × 11 selected bits at the beginning of the entropy buffer. It does not hash your input together with an independent full-length random secret. The OS supplies ENT − 11n bits, with ENT = 128 or 256. Count zero is equivalent to OS-only entropy.

If the prefix is predictable, only the remaining OS bits are unpredictable. For a 12-word phrase with 11 prefix words, that is 7 OS bits; for 24 words with 23 prefix words, it is 3. Fair independently generated prefix bits can contribute their full entropy, but a verification checkbox cannot establish that their source was random.

Raw mode consumes exactly ENT bits and adds no OS randomness. Bias, dependence, reuse and transcription errors all matter. Repeated clicks, personal sentences and guessed word sequences are unsuitable sources. The English BIP39 checksum detects some errors; it cannot assess entropy quality or prove the source was fair.
airvault-note_entropy: Changing the source, length or entry method clears the current entropy entry. Finish and record one attempt before changing these controls. Never use the public examples in these instructions for real funds.
airvault-guide_paths_basic:
A derivation path is the address-selection instruction under a wallet identity. The same recovery phrase can produce many accounts. A different path can produce a different address, even when the network and phrase stay the same.

For a new account, leave the suggested path unchanged. When restoring an account from another wallet, use the path that wallet actually used. A label such as Savings is only a name and does not select a different cryptographic account.
airvault-steps_paths:
Select the signing identity and Network in Accounts. Selecting a network fills in its suggested path.
Use the suggested path for a first account, or enter an exact previously recorded path when recovering an address.
Choose Derive account. Open Details and record the network, identity and path with your recovery notes.
Compare the resulting address with a known address from the original wallet if you are recovering funds.
airvault-result_paths: The same phrase, passphrase, network and supported path reproduce the same account address. Changing a label does not create a new address.
airvault-guide_paths_advanced:
BIP32 describes hierarchical derivation; an apostrophe marks a hardened child index. For example, the Bitcoin native SegWit default m/84'/0'/0'/0/0 selects the first external address in account zero under that convention. Test networks use their own defaults.

Path conventions and supported derivation algorithms vary across chains. Do not blindly copy a Bitcoin path into another adapter. AirVault derives explicitly selected accounts; an empty result after restoration is not proof that the phrase has no funds. Recover the original identity, path and network before diagnosing missing funds.

For compatibility, preserve address type and passphrase as well as the path. A known address comparison is a useful end-to-end derivation check. Keep these public derivation details separate from transaction descriptions, which do not control derivation.
airvault-note_paths: Repeatedly deriving the same identity, network and path does not create independent keys. Use the correct new path when you intentionally need another address.
airvault-guide_receive_basic: You receive funds by sharing an account address. You do not need to reveal a recovery phrase, private key, vault password or BIP39 passphrase to receive a payment. Address derivation works Offline.
airvault-steps_receive:
Open Accounts and derive an account from the intended wallet identity on the intended network.
Copy the account address. Check the full address against the sender's destination field, especially after pasting.
Tell the sender the exact network and asset. For tokens, confirm the network and contract or mint address too.
For a new setup, send a small test amount first. Confirm it on the correct network before sending more.
Use a trusted provider or explorer on the connected computer to check confirmation status.
airvault-result_receive: The payment belongs to the keys behind that address once accepted by the network. AirVault's local Activity page is not a complete list of incoming payments.
airvault-guide_receive_advanced:
An address identifies a destination under a chain's rules; matching textual formats do not establish matching networks. EVM chains often reuse an address while maintaining separate state and chain IDs. Asset identity includes the network and, for tokens, the contract or mint.

Verify public-account exports against the signer before using a Proxy address. A substituted watch-only address can redirect incoming payments without revealing a private key. Provider queries disclose address information, even when performed by a watch-only profile.
airvault-note_receive: An unsolicited request to enter your recovery phrase to receive or unlock a payment is not part of this workflow.
airvault-guide_online_basic: Online mode prepares and signs a transfer on the same computer. You still review and approve the transaction before signing, then broadcast it to the network. Preparing or signing alone does not send funds.
airvault-steps_online:
Open Settings, select Online, confirm with the vault password and Save. Choose the provider for your account's network if a custom endpoint is needed.
Open Prepare transfer. Select the account and asset, enter the recipient and amount, and choose Load network data (Fetch UTXOs for Bitcoin) to fill the required chain-specific fields. Check the values before proceeding.
Prepare the request. In Signing requests, open its review and check the actual recipient, asset, amount and fee.
Confirm the review and provide the vault password and any required custom root password to sign.
Review the signed result, then use Broadcast. Record the transaction ID and check its confirmation status.
airvault-result_online: A successful broadcast returns a transaction identifier. Inclusion and finality happen on the network afterward.
airvault-guide_online_advanced:
Online combines provider access and local key use in one process. The transaction inspection remains the approval boundary: friendly labels and descriptions do not substitute for decoded transaction fields.

Chain preparation may fetch UTXOs, nonces, recent blockhashes, runtime context or fee data. These can become stale between preparation and broadcast. A rejected transaction may need fresh preparation and another review; avoid repeated blind broadcasts when the initial outcome is unknown.

A token transfer may require native coin for fees. A displayed token symbol is metadata, not proof of contract identity. Read network-specific fields and the contract or mint before approval.
airvault-note_online: If broadcasting times out, first check the transaction ID and address history. A timeout does not prove the transaction was never accepted.
airvault-guide_exchange_basic:
Offline file exchange separates the computer that holds private keys from the computer that contacts the network. Use the same AirVault binary on each computer, with a separate profile for each role.

.avpub contains public accounts. .avreq contains an unsigned signing request. .avsig contains the signed response. None of these files is an encrypted vault backup.
airvault-steps_exchange:
On the isolated signer, create or import the wallet, derive accounts and keep Offline mode selected.
From Accounts, choose Export public accounts. Move the .avpub file to the connected computer and import it into a fresh Proxy profile.
On the Proxy, prepare the transfer. Open Signing requests and export the .avreq request.
Move the request to the signer and use Import file. Review all transaction fields on the signer, then approve and sign.
Export the .avsig response and move it back to the Proxy. Import it, review the signed result and broadcast.
Keep the request and response until the broadcast outcome is known. Check confirmation using the connected computer.
airvault-result_exchange: The Proxy can send the signed transaction while the recovery secret stays on the signer.
airvault-guide_exchange_advanced:
Public bundles disclose addresses, public keys, paths and token metadata. Requests carry transaction bytes plus contextual data; responses bind to a particular request digest. Treat imported files and media as untrusted, even when created by your other computer.

Approval is short-lived and tied to reviewed data. Mutation or re-preparation requires fresh review. A Solana blockhash or account-chain nonce can expire or change during transport; recreate stale requests on the connected side.

Use separate physical hosts for a real air gap. --data-dir can run separate disposable profiles on one machine to rehearse the workflow, but that does not isolate the signer from that machine's network or malware.
airvault-note_exchange: Never move an .avvault backup or recovery phrase to the Proxy just to make signing work. Recheck that the signer has the right identity, account and derivation path.
airvault-guide_fees_basic:
A network fee pays for processing a transaction. It is separate from the amount sent to the recipient. The amount and fee fields use the units shown next to them; do not assume every number is a whole coin.

Bitcoin-like networks spend previous outputs, called UTXOs. A transaction consumes those inputs, sends the requested amount and returns any change to a wallet address. Account-based networks use fields such as a nonce, gas limit or sequence instead.
airvault-steps_fees:
Choose the correct account and asset in Prepare transfer. Load current network data when that action is offered.
Check the units for the payment and fee. A satoshi is 0.00000001 BTC; gas price and other base-unit fields are not whole coins.
Review the selected inputs, recipient outputs and change. Check that the total fee is reasonable for the payment.
Keep enough native coin to pay the fee even when sending a token. If the transaction is rejected, inspect the error and refresh network state before trying again.
airvault-result_fees: The review separates the payment from the fee. Signing approves those transaction bytes, including the fee-related fields.
airvault-guide_fees_advanced:
For a UTXO transaction, fee equals total input value minus total output value. Change is an output and should return to an account you control. A high absolute fee and a high fee rate are different checks; inspect both when available.

Gas limit bounds execution work, while gas price or fee caps determine its cost. Nonces and sequences order account transactions. XRP destination tags and Cosmos memos can identify the intended beneficiary at a shared deposit address; obtain required values from the recipient.

Provider estimates and fetched inputs are not trustworthy merely because they arrived over TLS. Review amounts, outpoints, change, destination and chain-specific limits. Some networks enforce minimum outputs, reserves or validity windows. Refresh state when the network says it is stale.
airvault-note_fees: Never resolve a fee error by entering arbitrary larger values without understanding their units and the resulting total.
airvault-guide_providers_basic: A provider is a server that supplies blockchain data or accepts a signed transaction for broadcast. Online and Proxy use providers; Offline blocks these requests. Changing the provider does not move funds or change the recovery phrase.
airvault-steps_providers:
Open Settings and choose Provider network. This selects which network's endpoint you are editing.
Enter the endpoint for that same network and the API type supported by AirVault. Use the published provider address, not a block explorer's ordinary web page.
Confirm the settings with the vault password and Save.
Return to Prepare transfer and load current data. Check the network and returned values before preparing the transaction.
airvault-result_providers: Future calls for the selected network use its saved endpoint. Other networks keep their own settings.
airvault-guide_providers_advanced:
Use a provider for the selected network: Esplora for Bitcoin; Blockbook API v2 for Litecoin, Dogecoin and Bitcoin Cash; JSON-RPC for EVM, Solana and XRP; WSS for Polkadot Hub; Cosmos REST; Tron FullNode HTTP; or Koios API v1 for Cardano. HTTPS is required except for localhost. Provider data is external and may be inaccurate. No connection is made until you request network data or approve a broadcast.

Adapters expect specific protocols: Bitcoin uses Esplora-style endpoints; EVM networks use JSON-RPC; other families use their chain adapter's API. Polkadot supports a WebSocket endpoint. A matching URL scheme alone does not make an arbitrary service compatible.

Providers see queries such as addresses and transaction identifiers. They can be unavailable, stale or misleading. Transport security protects a connection, not the truth of a balance, fee estimate or chain state. The signer still needs to review what the transaction actually authorizes.

A Proxy does not provide an anonymous transport layer or a general HTTP proxy. Its purpose is to keep private keys out of the network-facing profile. For endpoint errors, check the network, protocol, service status and credentials required by that provider without sharing secrets in logs.
airvault-note_providers: Never put a recovery phrase or private key in a provider URL. Provider configuration is not a wallet recovery method.
airvault-guide_activity_basic: Activity records operations performed in this AirVault profile, such as signing and broadcasting. It helps connect a request to its transaction ID. It is not a complete blockchain explorer and does not continuously prove that a payment is confirmed.
airvault-steps_activity:
Open Activity and find the operation by time or request identifier.
For a broadcast event, use its transaction ID to check the correct network on the connected computer.
If you only see a signing event, return to Signing requests and export or broadcast the signed response as appropriate.
If the network outcome is uncertain, check the transaction ID before preparing a duplicate payment.
airvault-result_activity: You can distinguish local approval and signing from network acceptance and later confirmation.
airvault-guide_activity_advanced:
A locally stored event is evidence of an application operation, not consensus finality. A successful provider response does not imply a permanent block inclusion, and an RPC timeout does not imply failure to submit.

Requests and responses are connected by identifiers and digests. Preserve relevant exchange files while diagnosing an uncertain result. Changing profiles changes the local history you see; restored backups contain only the activity saved at backup time.
airvault-note_activity: A missing incoming payment in Activity does not establish that the address has no funds. Check the correct network with an independent source.
airvault-guide_backup_basic: An encrypted .avvault backup preserves the vault's stored wallets, identities and account details. A recovery phrase is a separate way to recover a wallet's keys. Keep both where appropriate, and test your recovery plan before relying on it.
airvault-steps_backup:
In Settings, open Encrypted backup. Enter the vault password, confirm the backup action and choose Create .avvault backup.
Store the file safely and record which password unlocks this backup. Keep any custom root passwords and BIP39 passphrases available separately.
To test a restore, launch AirVault with a fresh profile directory. On Windows, an example is AirVault.exe --data-dir C:\AirVaultProfiles\RestoreTest.
On the new-vault screen, enter the backup's vault password. Open Restore encrypted backup and leave the verification-only option selected for an initial check.
After a successful check, repeat with verification-only unchecked to install the backup in that fresh profile. Unlock it, compare known addresses and test the identities you need.
airvault-result_backup: A successful restore in a fresh profile reproduces the data stored in the backup. Creating a backup does not update older backup files.
airvault-guide_backup_advanced:
Backups retain encrypted key material and saved metadata. Restoring requires the password used when that backup was created; changing the current vault password does not re-encrypt older exported copies. Preserve a known-good copy while validating a replacement.

A dry run verifies the backup without installing it. Installation refuses an already initialized profile to avoid overwriting another vault. Use an explicitly new --data-dir for rehearsals. Testing on the same host checks recovery mechanics, not disaster resilience.

Phrase-only recovery also needs the exact BIP39 passphrase, network and derivation path for each identity. A custom root password protects the stored root wrapper, whereas the recovery phrase can reconstruct the underlying wallet independently of that wrapper.
airvault-note_backup: Do not delete your original profile after a single successful file check. Verify addresses and needed signing identities in the restored profile first.
airvault-guide_locking_basic:
Auto-lock ends an unlocked session after inactivity. Enter seconds in Settings, or enter -1 for Never. Never disables the inactivity timer only; closing AirVault still ends the session.

Lock on focus loss is a separate option. If it is enabled, switching to another window locks the vault even with -1 selected. Manual Lock vault and sleep/resume protections also remain active.
airvault-steps_locking:
Open Settings and find Auto-lock after inactivity (seconds).
Enter -1 for no inactivity lock, or an interval between 30 and 3600 seconds.
Choose whether Lock on focus loss should be enabled. Enter the vault password, confirm and Save.
Use Lock vault whenever you step away. After closing and reopening AirVault, enter the vault password to unlock again.
airvault-result_locking: The chosen setting persists in this vault. -1 does not keep a vault unlocked after the application exits.
airvault-guide_locking_advanced:
The native session enforces the inactivity policy. -1 is the explicit sentinel; zero and other negative values are rejected. Activity from the interface refreshes the idle timer, while the session tick separately checks for long pauses.

A missed tick of more than 15 seconds triggers a lock to handle sleep or process stalls. Windows session power events also request locking. These protections are independent of the inactivity sentinel and focus-loss option.

Locking discards the active vault, pending ceremony and signing approval from the session. It does not erase externally copied secrets, clipboard history, swap or other software's memory. The next launch reads encrypted storage and starts locked.
airvault-note_locking: If -1 appears not to work, check Lock on focus loss and whether the computer slept or the process paused.
airvault-guide_integrity_basic:
About shows three different identities: the application version, a source fingerprint computed during the build, and the SHA-256 of the application file currently running. The source fingerprint changes when included source files change, even before changes are committed.

A file hash is useful for comparing a download with a known release. Use a checksum obtained from a source you trust independently of the file you are checking.
airvault-steps_integrity:
Open About from the unlock screen or the sidebar. Read the version, version hash and current binary SHA-256.
Obtain the expected AirVault.exe checksum for that exact release and platform. Do not compare the ZIP's checksum to the EXE's checksum.
Paste the 64-character EXE checksum into Compare with a trusted SHA-256. A match means the bytes match that checksum.
Choose Recalculate hash to read the application file again. For an independent Windows check, run Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 with the full path to AirVault.exe in PowerShell.
If the expected and actual values differ, stop using that file until you understand the difference.
airvault-result_integrity: You can identify the source used for the build and compare the current executable with a trusted reference.
airvault-guide_integrity_advanced:
The source fingerprint hashes sorted, length-framed paths and bytes for application source, manifests, dependency locks, build support, bundled public assets and configuration inputs. It includes uncommitted and newly added files in those inputs. Git revision and the local-change marker are displayed separately.

The runtime digest streams the bytes at the current executable path on each request; it is not an embedded expected checksum. BUILD-INFO.json in the portable package records the corresponding build metadata and packaged executable hash. File metadata and the build timestamp can make separately built binaries differ even for the same source hash.

This is an integrity comparison, not code signing or remote attestation. A modified application can lie about its own digest. The EXE hash does not cover WebView2Loader.dll, the installed WebView runtime, in-memory patches, the operating system or your vault. Use an external hash tool and an authenticated release reference for independent verification.
airvault-note_integrity: A checksum supplied only alongside an untrusted download can be replaced with it. Matching those two files alone does not establish authenticity.
airvault-guide_troubleshooting_basic: Start with the exact error and the page where it occurred. Keep recovery words and passwords out of screenshots and support messages. Public test wallets are useful for reproducing problems without exposing real funds.
airvault-steps_troubleshooting:
If phrase verification fails, keep the text in place and check spelling, order and word count. Use one numbered word per line, or unnumbered words separated by spaces. Four-letter prefixes are accepted; three-letter words must be complete.
If a generated phrase's five-minute confirmation window expired, cancel and start a fresh ceremony. Do not receive funds for an unfinished wallet.
If Proxy is disabled, use a fresh profile with no private roots. If Prepare transfer is missing, check whether the profile is Offline.
If a provider request fails, check its network and endpoint in Settings. Refresh nonce, blockhash or other state before rebuilding an expired request.
If AirVault cannot find WebView2Loader.dll, extract the entire portable ZIP with the DLL beside AirVault.exe, or use the installer. Do not move just the EXE out of its folder.
If a recovered address differs, check the passphrase identity, network, path and address convention before using it.
airvault-result_troubleshooting: Input errors can be corrected without clearing the phrase field. State-related transaction errors require a fresh review of any rebuilt request.
airvault-guide_troubleshooting_advanced:
Separate input validation, vault authentication, provider transport, transaction inspection and network rejection. A checksum failure concerns mnemonic data; a wrong-password failure concerns encrypted storage. Neither implies a provider problem.

For an uncertain broadcast, query by the signed transaction ID before resubmitting or making a replacement. For a missing restored account, compare derivation inputs with the original wallet rather than generating random paths.

Report the application version, source hash, target platform, operation and sanitized error text. Do not include the vault file, recovery phrase, raw secret input, passwords or a secret-bearing clipboard dump. Exchange files contain transaction and account information and should also be treated as private.
airvault-note_troubleshooting: Do not delete a profile or overwrite recovery material to troubleshoot an error. Keep a known-good backup and work in a disposable profile.
airvault-guide_glossary_basic:
Vault: the encrypted local file that holds wallets, identities, account details and settings.

Wallet or root: the recovery secret from which accounts are derived. Recovery phrase: the ordered words used to reconstruct that secret.

Signing identity: a wallet used with a particular BIP39 passphrase. Default is the identity with no extra BIP39 passphrase.

Account: a saved address on one network, derived from an identity and path. Watch-only: public information without signing keys.

Entropy: unpredictable input used to create a secret. Checksum: a short consistency check; it does not measure how random the input was.

Provider: a network service used for blockchain data and broadcasting. Proxy: AirVault's public-only role on the connected computer.

Signing: authorizing transaction bytes with a private key. Broadcasting: sending the signed transaction to the network. Confirmation: inclusion and subsequent acceptance under that network's rules.
airvault-guide_glossary_advanced:
Root encryption and identity derivation are distinct: changing a vault password re-protects storage; changing a BIP39 passphrase changes the derived identity.

A digest is a fixed-length hash of bytes. A signature authenticates a message under a key. A digest alone does not identify an author.

UTXO means unspent transaction output. Nonce or sequence commonly orders account transactions. A derivation path selects keys in a hierarchy; a chain ID selects an EVM network. A token contract or mint identifies an asset on its network.

.avpub is a public-account bundle; .avreq is an unsigned request; .avsig is a signed response; .avvault is an encrypted backup. Testnet, devnet and similar networks use separate test assets.
airvault-guide_whitepaper_basic:
The original Bitcoin whitepaper is included below as an offline PDF. It introduces a peer-to-peer payment system and explains how a network can agree on transaction history without a central operator.

Read the introduction and conclusion first, then the sections on transactions and proof of work. Use the glossary for unfamiliar terms. This is background reading; the AirVault walkthroughs explain the application's buttons and file exchange.
airvault-guide_whitepaper_advanced:
The paper describes transaction ownership, timestamping, proof of work, incentives and a simplified verification approach. Its attacker model and probability discussion are useful foundations for understanding confirmations.

It predates modern wallet practices such as hierarchical key derivation, mnemonic backups and current transaction formats. Use current protocol documentation for implementation details; the paper is not an AirVault security audit or a specification for other chains.
airvault-page_multisig: Create a Bitcoin wallet that needs signatures from multiple independent keys. Start with 2-of-3, exchange only public cosigner keys, compare the configuration on every signer, and save its configuration before receiving funds.
airvault-multiYourKeyHelp: Create a separate recovery phrase on each signer first. Select its identity here and export only the public cosigner key. A watch-only coordinator needs no recovery phrase. Never collect the signers’ recovery phrases on one computer.
airvault-multiSetupHelp: Paste one public cosigner key per line, including your own. Choose how many signatures are required. All signers must register the same threshold, network, cosigners and address index. Select your local signing identity above, or Watch only on the coordinator.
airvault-multiCosignersHint: Use [fingerprint/48h/coinh/accounth/2h]xpub or tpub. Include 2–15 distinct cosigners. Default: 2 signatures from 3 keys.
airvault-multiCompare: Compare this address and every cosigner with the other devices before using the wallet.
airvault-multiBackupHint: Save the configuration after registering. Keep a separate recovery phrase and any BIP39 passphrase for each signer. Recovery needs the configuration for every cosigner plus enough independent keys to meet the threshold.
airvault-multiConfirm: I checked the threshold, network, address and every cosigner against the other devices.
airvault-multiRegistered: Multisig account registered. Save its configuration before receiving funds.
airvault-multiPsbtHelp: Import an unsigned native SegWit single-signature PSBT, or an unfinalized native SegWit multisig PSBT. Include full previous transactions. Export PSBTs for signing in another wallet; once signing is complete, a raw .txn export opens directly in Sparrow.
airvault-multiSigned: Signature added. Export the PSBT for the next signer or coordinator.
airvault-multiProgressHelp: Each input must reach its own signature threshold. Imported signatures are checked against the transaction and registered cosigners. Only a complete, independently verified transaction can be broadcast.
airvault-guide_multisig_basic:
A 2-of-3 wallet has three independent keys and needs any two to spend. One lost key does not prevent recovery; someone with just one key cannot spend. Multisig creates new Bitcoin addresses. It does not protect coins already held at your old single-key address until you move them.

Use three separate signers with independently generated recovery phrases. Keep the signers and their backups in different places. A connected coordinator can hold just the public configuration in Proxy mode. For practice, use a Bitcoin test network and disposable phrases first.

The public cosigner key is safe to exchange for setup, but reveals wallet information. It begins with an origin in square brackets and an xpub or tpub. Never exchange recovery phrases, private keys or passphrases.
airvault-steps_multisig:
On each signer, create and verify a different recovery phrase under Create or import. If using a BIP39 passphrase, create that identity and back it up separately.
Open Bitcoin multisig. Choose the same Bitcoin network on every device, select the local identity, leave the BIP48 account index at 0 for your first wallet, and choose Show public cosigner key.
Exchange those public keys. On each device, enter a label, set Signatures required to 2 and paste all three public keys, one per line. Leave Receive and address index 0 selected.
Choose Review configuration. Compare all complete public keys, origins, threshold, network and the displayed receive address through a trusted channel. Do not rely only on the short fingerprints.
Confirm and register on every signer, selecting that device’s local identity. On a coordinator, select Watch only and register the same configuration.
Save a configuration backup on every device. Complete a recovery rehearsal, then try receiving and spending a small amount before transferring more.
airvault-result_multisig: All devices show the same address for the same configuration and index. Each signer holds only its own secret. The coordinator can prepare transactions but cannot add signatures.
airvault-note_multisig: Separate profiles on one computer are convenient for testing but do not provide the security separation of independent devices. Two derived keys from one recovery phrase are not two independent backups.
airvault-guide_multisig_advanced:
AirVault uses native SegWit P2WSH wsh(sortedmulti(M,...)) with BIP67 ordering and BIP48 origins m/48'/coin'/account'/2'. Coin type is 0 for Bitcoin mainnet and 1 for the Bitcoin test networks. Public children use branch 0 for receive or 1 for change, followed by an unhardened address index. Keys are sorted at each child index.

Configure 2–15 cosigners and a threshold of 1 through N; the default is 2-of-3. Duplicate keys and root fingerprints are rejected. Fingerprints are short identifiers, not authentication; local ownership is established by deriving and comparing the complete account xpub. Imported PSBT origins never select arbitrary secret derivation paths.

Cosigner entries accept standard xpub/tpub serialization with BIP48 origins. This flow covers native SegWit multisig only: legacy P2SH, nested P2SH-P2WSH, Taproot/MuSig, mixed single-key/multisig inputs and other chains use different policies and are not handled by this multisig flow.

AirVault saves individual address indices as accounts. Prepare next address fills in the next index for review; register it on each signer and the coordinator before receiving or spending from it. To use a change branch, select Change explicitly. The receive/change ranged descriptors in the backup let compatible wallets reconstruct other indices. AirVault does not automatically discover all used indices or scan a descriptor range.
airvault-guide_multisigSigning_basic:
Signing happens in rounds. The first signer adds a signature without making the transaction spendable. A second independent signer reviews the same transaction and adds another. For 2-of-3, any two keys can complete the transaction. Every input must have enough signatures.

Use PSBT files for these rounds. The PSBT contains transaction details and signatures, never the recovery phrase. On each device, compare the destination, amount, fee, wallet and change address with your own intended payment. A green or complete status is not a substitute for this review.
airvault-steps_multisigSigning:
On the coordinator, register the same multisig accounts, including any receive or change indices being spent. In Online or Proxy mode, prepare a Bitcoin transfer from the multisig account.
Open Signing requests and export its PSBT. Transfer it to the first offline signer.
On the signer, select the matching Bitcoin network under Multisig PSBT exchange and import the file. If the wallet or index is unknown, register its verified configuration first.
Review the outputs, fees and per-input signature counts. Enter the vault password, approve and add the local signature. Export the updated PSBT.
Import that updated PSBT on another independent signer and repeat the review and signing. Parallel copies signed by different devices can also be imported into the coordinator and combined.
Import the resulting PSBT on the coordinator. Review the complete transaction. When all inputs have enough signatures, a final response appears and Online or Proxy mode offers Broadcast.
airvault-result_multisigSigning: The request remains pending after the first signature. After enough valid signatures arrive for every input, AirVault builds and verifies a complete transaction. Offline mode never broadcasts.
airvault-note_multisigSigning: A .avreq is the original request and does not carry later signing rounds. Export PSBT to transfer current signatures. A .avsig is a complete response tied to an AirVault request ID; returning the PSBT lets a coordinator with its own request ID finalize locally.
airvault-guide_multisigSigning_advanced:
PSBT version 0 imports accept binary or base64 files with the .psbt extension. Only unfinalized native SegWit sortedmulti inputs are accepted. Supply the full previous transaction for every input, the witness script, and SIGHASH_ALL. Some wallets export only witness UTXOs; use their option to include full previous transactions. Finalized PSBTs must be re-exported before finalization.

AirVault verifies previous transaction hashes and values, witness-script commitments, registered policies, every partial ECDSA signature and low-S encoding. Unknown signers, conflicting signatures, changed transactions and insufficient thresholds are rejected. Each merge adds verified signatures only; it does not replace local keys or wallet policy. Existing approvals are invalidated when PSBT data is imported.

Unsigned transaction bytes and Bitcoin network identify an existing local request for merging. Different destinations or fees create a different transaction requiring fresh review. Request-envelope checksums detect file corruption but do not authenticate a counterparty. Missing network metadata is why you must explicitly select the network on import.

Finalization orders signatures by the sorted script keys and supplies exactly the required count. A separate verifier checks the final witness, transaction outputs, input sequences and signature hashes before a response can be broadcast. Fees are estimated using the threshold and script size; the displayed rate is an estimate until signatures are finalized.
airvault-guide_multisigBackup_basic:
A recovery phrase is only one part of a multisig backup. Keep the public wallet configuration for ALL cosigners, even a cosigner whose private key is lost. The configuration tells recovery software which keys must sign and how to rebuild the wallet’s addresses.

For each signer, back up its recovery phrase and exact BIP39 passphrase if used. Keep these secrets separated so a single theft, fire or compromise cannot expose or destroy the threshold number of keys. Record who holds each signer and how to reach them without publishing the secrets.

Save configuration backup writes an .avmulti file containing the network, threshold, every cosigner xpub and origin, receive/change descriptors and the saved address index. It contains no private keys. Keep multiple copies and a readable copy of the descriptors, plus a record of every used branch/index and a known receive address. Update your records when you add addresses.

An encrypted .avvault backup is useful too, but needs its vault password and any custom root passwords. Keep these credentials recoverable separately. A BIP39 passphrase changes the wallet; a vault or custom root password only unlocks encrypted storage.
airvault-steps_multisigBackup:
After registration, choose Save configuration backup. Store copies separately from each other. Keep each signer’s secret backup separately from enough other secrets to spend.
Record threshold, network, all public key origins, both descriptors, used address indices and a known funded address. The file’s checksum catches corruption; comparing trusted addresses catches a substituted configuration.
Rehearse on disposable test-network funds first. Restore one signer’s phrase and passphrase on a fresh offline profile. Load the configuration, select that identity, review and register it. Compare the resulting address to the original.
Repeat on enough independent devices to reach the threshold. Restore the public configuration on a fresh coordinator. Re-register all used receive/change indices; use a compatible descriptor wallet for range discovery when needed.
Create and sign a small test payment through the restored signers and verify confirmation. Confirm you can do this without relying on the original vault files before trusting the backup plan.
airvault-result_multisigBackup: You can rebuild the same addresses from the public configuration and spend using the threshold number of independently restored signers. A configuration backup alone can only watch addresses.
airvault-note_multisigBackup: In 2-of-3, losing one private key is survivable only if two usable keys and the complete public configuration remain. Two lost keys normally mean permanent loss of access. Back up all three secrets independently rather than planning to lose one.
airvault-guide_multisigBackup_advanced:
The recovery set is M usable private cosigner roots with their exact BIP39 passphrases, plus the N-cosigner wallet policy: script type, threshold, all account xpubs, root fingerprints, origin paths, network and derivation branches/indices. Individual seeds do not identify absent cosigners’ xpubs or the original threshold. Keep the full configuration even when you have M seeds.

.avmulti includes BIP380-checksummed receive/change ranged descriptors and a SHA-256 consistency checksum. These are integrity checks, not signatures or proof of trusted origin. A malicious replacement can have a valid checksum. Authenticate configuration during setup and verify a previously recorded address during recovery. Descriptor-capable recovery tools can import the public descriptors and combine independently restored keys; handling secrets depends on the recovery tool.

AirVault’s account list tracks explicit indices. The configuration’s saved branch/index recreates that entry; the ranged descriptors reconstruct the address family. Record the highest used receive and change indices, relevant transaction IDs and an approximate creation date to help recovery scans. Discovering an address and spending its UTXOs also requires blockchain data.

An encrypted vault backup retains local identities, configuration and signing progress but is not a replacement for separate seed and configuration backups. Recovery from BIP39 seeds does not require the old AirVault vault password; recovery from an encrypted vault file does. A custom root password is required to unlock wrapped roots in that file. Test all paths you intend to rely on.
airvault-guide_multisigRisks_basic:
Multisig can reduce the damage from one lost or stolen key, but adds setup and recovery work. With M-of-N, an attacker who gains M keys can spend; losing more than N minus M keys can make the funds inaccessible. A 1-of-N threshold has no protection against one stolen key. N-of-N tolerates no lost or unavailable signers.

Keeping enough keys on one computer or in one place defeats the intended separation. Shared malware, cloud backup accounts, devices or custodians can become a common point of failure. An unavailable cosigner can delay spending even when no key is technically lost.

A dishonest coordinator can propose a payment to an attacker. Every signer must check the destination and amount independently. Compare the wallet configuration and receiving address before funding: a substituted xpub can give an attacker a place in your wallet.

Changing a label, deleting an account or creating a new configuration does not revoke an old key. If a signer is lost or compromised, use the remaining threshold to move funds to a newly verified wallet with replacement keys.
airvault-steps_multisigRisks:
Choose a threshold that balances theft resistance and the number of signers you can reliably recover. Work through a lost-key scenario before funding.
Keep signers and backups separated, with trusted instructions for recovery and inheritance. Do not put threshold secrets in one shared cloud account.
Compare each receive address and review each payment on independent devices. Use a small test transaction first.
If a key may be compromised, assess whether enough independent keys remain safe. Create and verify a new wallet, then move funds with the existing threshold; the old configuration cannot rotate keys in place.
Review your backup and signer availability periodically, without typing recovery phrases into websites or the connected coordinator.
airvault-result_multisigRisks: Your setup has a deliberate plan for theft, key loss, unavailable signers, recovery and replacement. No single configuration can remove all of these risks.
airvault-note_multisigRisks: Anyone who obtains a fully signed transaction may broadcast it. Partial signatures can also be combined later with other signatures for that same transaction. Treat signed PSBTs as spending approvals, not disposable drafts.
airvault-guide_multisigRisks_advanced:
Multisig enforces a script threshold, not independence of operators or entropy. Distinct fingerprints and xpubs cannot prove that the devices, backups, software supply chain or administrators are independent. Shared roots, leaked BIP39 passphrases and common operational failures can collapse the assumed M-of-N protection.

Public xpubs and descriptors disclose the wallet’s address family and spending policy. Keep them private for financial privacy even though they cannot spend by themselves. Avoid exposing unhardened child private keys alongside an account xpub; BIP32 relationships can endanger the parent private key. AirVault exports public configuration, never child private keys.

P2WSH multisig witnesses are larger than a single-key SegWit spend and cost more to spend. Bitcoin network fee conditions and the chosen number of signatures matter. Multisig does not provide a timelock, spending limit, cancellation service or automatic key rotation. Replacement means moving coins to a new script while enough old keys remain available.

SIGHASH_ALL binds the reviewed transaction’s outputs and inputs. Signatures for a changed fee or destination need a fresh signing round. Signed transactions do not expire simply because the review dialog closes or the vault locks; if the inputs remain unspent, a retained completed transaction may still be broadcast. If fewer than the threshold secrets survive, there is no administrator reset or recovery bypass.
airvault-multiWaiting: Waiting for another cosigner. Close this review and export the PSBT to continue on another signer.
airvault-page_inspector: Inspect serialized payloads locally, compare their bytes and check protocol integrity before signing or sending.
airvault-inspectorHelp: Open any file up to 8 MiB or paste hex/Base64. Recognized payloads are divided into colored fields. Hover or focus a byte for its meaning; click to pin it. Inspection reads bytes and never signs or sends them.
airvault-inspectorPaste: Paste hex, Base64 or an AirVault envelope
airvault-inspectorLimit: Any file type · up to 8 MiB · processed locally
airvault-inspectorCopyFailed: Could not copy the hex. Check clipboard access and retry.
airvault-inspectorOffsetError: Enter a byte offset inside this document, in decimal or 0x hexadecimal.
airvault-inspectorHover: Hover or focus bytes to inspect a field. Click to pin its explanation; Escape unpins. Arrow keys move between bytes.
airvault-inspectorRefine: Showing the first 80 matches. Refine the search to find another field.
airvault-guide_inspector_basic:
Use Payload inspector to see what a transaction or signing file actually contains. It works locally in Offline, Proxy and Online modes. Choose Open any file, or expand the paste area to inspect hex, Base64 or an AirVault envelope. Opening a file here does not import it into your vault.

The byte document selector separates the original file from decoded payloads and embedded transactions. Hexadecimal shows each byte as two digits; ASCII shows printable characters and uses a dot for other bytes. Both views highlight the same field. Hover over a byte, use the arrow keys, or click a field name to read its purpose and expected contents. Click a byte to pin the helper, then Unpin or press Escape to follow another field.

Check a request on the Proxy before exporting it and again on the Offline signer. Inspect the signed response on the connected computer before broadcasting. Signing requests and their review dialog both include Inspect payload. After importing an AirVault exchange file or PSBT, its inspection opens automatically.
