Failed imports retain their inspection so you can examine the problem.
airvault-steps_inspector:
Open Payload inspector and choose a file, or paste its text representation.
Choose a byte document; for an AirVault request, inspect Envelope payload as well as the original envelope.
Expand failed checks and inspect the highlighted header, inputs, outputs and signature data.
Compare the destination, amount, network, fee and file hash with an independently trusted source.
Repeat the review on the other computer. Continue signing or broadcasting through Signing requests only after checking the intended transaction.
airvault-result_inspector: You can identify byte ranges, read their meaning and see exactly which integrity checks passed, failed or were not performed. Unsupported data stays available as raw bytes.
airvault-note_inspector: A matching checksum detects corruption; an attacker can replace bytes and calculate a new checksum. No checksum establishes that a destination is yours or that a transaction is safe. Raw Bitcoin transactions and PSBTs do not carry an embedded file checksum. Never treat decoding as approval to sign.
airvault-guide_inspector_advanced:
The native inspector accepts up to 8 MiB of untrusted bytes without a vault dependency or network access. Automatic detection recognizes raw Bitcoin legacy/SegWit transactions, PSBTv0, unencrypted Bitcoin v1 P2P messages and EVM legacy/EIP-2930/EIP-1559 RLP transactions. Force a decoder when a damaged header prevents recognition. Arbitrary files, unsupported PSBT versions, unknown extensions and encrypted BIP324 streams remain inspectable as opaque bytes. This tool does not parse PCAP, IP or TCP containers; extract the reassembled Bitcoin application stream first.

Offsets always refer to the selected document. The original file hash includes its exact whitespace and text encoding. Decoding hex/Base64 or an AirVault payload creates another document with offsets starting at zero. Embedded PSBT transactions are separate documents, not byte offsets into the original encoded file. Large views are paged; detailed parsing is bounded to 24,000 fields per document, 32 documents and limited nested payloads.

Checks include canonical CompactSize integers, complete transaction framing, output money bounds, duplicate outpoints, PSBTv0 key uniqueness/map counts/native parsing, previous-transaction txid/output binding, agreement of witness and non-witness UTXOs, and supplied P2SH/P2WSH script commitments. A PSBT fee is reported only from supplied consistent UTXO values; witness-only values are not independently authenticated. P2P messages verify declared payload lengths, command padding and the first four bytes of double SHA-256. Common message bodies are decoded, including tx, block, version, ping/pong, inventory, headers and locators; blocks also check merkle and witness commitments.

EVM decoding checks canonical RLP, field counts, integer/address sizes and access-list structure, and segments function selectors and ABI argument words. It does not resolve a contract ABI or execute the contract. AirVault envelopes use the native request/response schema and compare SHA-256 of decoded payload bytes. Other AirVault chain operations are inspectable as typed JSON, with their envelope integrity checked.

The inspector does not execute Bitcoin scripts, recover EVM signatures, establish chain membership, look up UTXO spend status or authenticate an envelope sender. A response requestDigest requires the original request to verify its binding. Existing signing review, registered-wallet checks and independent response verification remain the authority for signing and broadcast.

Stored request/response inspection shows the canonical export bytes, which can differ from whitespace in the imported JSON file. Open the file itself when comparing an exact original-file checksum.
airvault-inspectorFailedChecks: Some protocol checks failed. Review the checks in each byte document before continuing.
airvault-guide_interoperability_basic:
AirVault can exchange standard Bitcoin PSBT files with Sparrow. You can open a PSBT or a complete raw transaction in Sparrow without importing your recovery phrase. Choose the same Bitcoin network in both applications. AirVault exchange envelopes (.avreq and .avsig) are for AirVault; Sparrow opens .psbt and .txn files.

Before signing, Export PSBT saves an unsigned transaction or the current multisig signing round. Once signing is complete, Export signed PSBT includes the signatures, and Export raw transaction saves a .txn file that Sparrow opens directly. Single-signature exports include the signature and public derivation information; multisig PSBT exports preserve collected signatures between devices. A raw transaction is available only after every input has enough verified signatures.

Unsigned native SegWit single-signature PSBTs and unfinalized native SegWit multisig PSBTs can be imported into AirVault. The corresponding accounts must be registered, and every input needs its full previous transaction. If another wallet removes that information or finalizes a PSBT, use its compatible unfinalized export for another AirVault signing round.
airvault-steps_interoperability:
In AirVault, open Signing requests and choose Export PSBT, Export signed PSBT or Export raw transaction.
In Sparrow, choose File → Open Transaction → File and select the .psbt or .txn file.
Review recipients, amounts, fees and signatures. A PSBT contains more information for offline fee review than a raw transaction.
To send an unsigned single-signature PSBT or a partial multisig PSBT back, save it from Sparrow as a binary PSBT before finalization.
In AirVault, choose the intended network and Import PSBT. Review it again before approving a signature.
Once complete, open the signed PSBT or raw transaction in Sparrow for an independent review.
airvault-result_interoperability: Sparrow can inspect AirVault signatures and final transactions, and AirVault can continue compatible unsigned or partial signing requests returned by Sparrow.
airvault-note_interoperability: Opening or exporting a transaction does not broadcast it. Only a complete, verified transaction can use raw export. Raw transactions do not contain the full previous-output data needed to verify every fee offline; keep the PSBT for detailed review. Never use the public seeds in the project test harness for real funds.
airvault-guide_interoperability_advanced:
PSBT exports use BIP174 version 0. For single-signature P2WPKH, AirVault reconstructs partial_sigs from the independently verified final witness, preserving the unsigned transaction, UTXOs and key origins. Export is derived from the stored response, including responses imported on a Proxy, so encrypted vaults created before this feature do not need a migration. P2WPKH input and known output origins are included when the registered account has BIP32 metadata.

Multisig signing rounds export their verified unfinalized P2WSH PSBT with collected signatures. If only an imported complete .avsig is available, AirVault constructs a standard finalized PSBT with final_script_witness and removes obsolete signing fields. The .txn export is lowercase hexadecimal UTF-8 of the complete network-serialized transaction, matching Sparrow’s Save Transaction convention. Both exports verify the stored response against the original request, scripts, signatures, amounts and network before writing. Incomplete multisig requests cannot export a raw transaction.

AirVault accepts unsigned native P2WPKH PSBTs and unfinalized native P2WSH sortedmulti PSBTs under its existing account registration, full non_witness_utxo and SIGHASH_ALL rules. Standard PSBT import invalidates any outstanding signing approval. Single-signature PSBT imports with the same network and unsigned transaction reuse the pending request without replacing its reviewed semantics. Imported key origins never direct private derivation.

A final raw transaction can be opened in Sparrow without a wallet, but its input amounts require previous transactions or a connected node. PSBT provides those values for offline comparison. A PSBT does not identify its Bitcoin network reliably; select the correct network on import. AirVault-specific request IDs and envelope bindings do not travel in the standard transaction serialization.
